title: Doers of the Word
subtitle: James in Poems & Pictures
author: Timothy Holt
beforeYouBegin:
James is a short letter of plain wisdom: trials and endurance, the rich and the poor, faith that works, a tongue that sets forests on fire, and a farmer waiting for rain.

This book walks through its five chapters in thirty short poems. Each poem sits beside a picture and under a single line of Scripture, so you can read it in an evening, or one page a morning.

The poems are not the Bible. They are one reader's response to it. Open the letter of James alongside this one, and let the real words have the last word.

parts.title: Doers of the Word
parts.epigraph: But be doers of the word, and not only hearers
parts.lightName: Light of Doers of the Word
parts.lightHint: Near 'the kiln' (James 1:2–4) in Part 1: Doers of the Word
parts.zh_epigraph: 只是你们要行道，不要单单听道

parts.title: Faith That Works
parts.epigraph: Even so faith, if it has no works, is dead in itself.
parts.lightHint: Near 'the good seat' (James 2:1–4) in Part 2: Faith That Works
parts.zh_epigraph: 这样，信心若没有行为就是死的。

parts.title: The Small Fire
parts.epigraph: But the wisdom that is from above is first pure, then peaceful, gentle, reasonable, full of mercy and good fruits
parts.lightHint: Near 'we all stumble' (James 3:1–2) in Part 3: The Small Fire
parts.zh_epigraph: 惟独从上头来的智慧，先是清洁，后是和平，温良柔顺，满有怜悯，多结善果

parts.epigraph: Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you.
parts.lightHint: Near 'open hands' (James 4:1–3) in Part 4: Draw Near
parts.zh_epigraph: 你们亲近神，神就必亲近你们。

parts.title: The Early and Late Rain
parts.epigraph: the farmer waits for the precious fruit of the earth
parts.lightName: Light of The Early and Late Rain
parts.lightHint: Near 'moth-eaten' (James 5:1–4) in Part 5: The Early and Late Rain
parts.zh_epigraph: 看哪，农夫忍耐等候地里宝贵的出产

paintings.title: the kiln
paintings.epigraph: “the testing of your faith produces endurance.”
paintings.poem:
count it joy, he says—
not the trial,
but what the trial is making.

clay doesn't enjoy the kiln.
but it comes out
able to hold water.

endurance is not
a feeling.
it is a shape
you are being fired into.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Imagine standing inside this frame beside the quiet centerpiece of “the kiln”: what hurry or noise in your week begins to fade when you hear, “it is a shape you are being fired into”?
paintings.zh_poem:
他说，都要以为大喜乐——
不是为试炼本身，
而是为试炼正在成全的事。

泥土并不喜欢窑炉，
但出窑之后，
它才盛得住水。

忍耐并不是
一种情绪；
它是你在烈火中
被烧制而成的器型。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 想象自己站在这幅画框里、守在《窑炉》那安静的画面中心：当你听见“它是你在烈火中被烧制而成的器型”时，你这一周里的哪些匆忙与喧嚣开始渐渐消退？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “因为知道你们的信心经过试验，就生忍耐。”

paintings.title: ask
paintings.epigraph: “let him ask of God, who gives to all liberally and without reproach”
paintings.poem:
if you don't know what to do,
ask.

he gives to everyone,
generously,
and never says
you should have known.

but ask like you mean it—
not like a wave
blown one way, then the other,
wanting the answer
and wanting to keep your options open.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Read the closing words aloud in the stillness: “but ask like you mean it— not like a wave blown one way, then the other, wanting the answer and wanting to keep your options open.” What part of your heart feels most searched or comforted by James 1:5–8 right now?
paintings.zh_title: 应当求那厚赐与众人的神
paintings.zh_poem:
如果你不知该如何行，
只管求问。

他厚赐与众人，
慷慨大方，
从不斥责说：
你早该知道了。

但求的时候要凭着信心——
不要像海中的波浪，
被风吹动翻腾，
既想要答案，
又想为自己留条后路。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在静默中轻声读出结尾的诗句：“但求的时候要凭着信心——不要像海中的波浪，被风吹动翻腾，既想要答案，又想为自己留条后路。”此刻，雅各书 1:5–8 最触动或最安慰你内心的是哪一部分？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “应当求那厚赐与众人、也不斥责人的神”

paintings.title: wildflower
paintings.epigraph: “like the flower in the grass, he will pass away”
paintings.poem:
the red flowers on the hillside
are beautiful for a week.

then the hot wind comes,
and the sun,
and by noon
they are straw.

so the rich man, too,
in the middle of his busy plans.

the poor brother can lift his head.
he was never counting
on flowers.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: In James 1:9–11, grace meets us right beside the quiet centerpiece of “wildflower”: how does the closing thought—“he was never counting on flowers”—steady your footing for the road ahead?
paintings.zh_poem:
山坡上的红花，
能绚烂一整个星期。

随后热风吹起，
太阳升上来，
不到正午，
便枯干如草。

那富足的人也是这样，
在他忙乱的筹算中渐渐衰残。

卑微的弟兄却可以抬起头来——
他从一开始，
就未曾指望过花朵。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在雅各书 1:9–11 中，恩典就在《草上的花》那安静的画面中心与我们相遇：结尾的深思——“他从一开始，就未曾指望过花朵”——如何为你前面的道路稳住脚步？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “因为他必要过去，如同草上的花一样。”

paintings.title: no shifting shadow
paintings.epigraph: “Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of lights”
paintings.poem:
the sun moves,
and the shadow on the sundial
moves with it.

morning, noon, evening—
every light we know
turns.

but the Father of lights
casts no shifting shadow.

every good thing in your hands this morning—
the bread, the breath, the friend—
came down from a hand
that does not change its mind.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: If today’s painting of “no shifting shadow” (James 1:16–17) hung beside the door you walk out of this morning, how would its final line—“every good thing in your hands this morning— the bread, the breath, the friend— came down from a hand that does not change its mind”—shape your choices?
paintings.zh_poem:
太阳移动，
日晷上的影儿
也随之移动。

清晨、正午、傍晚——
我们所知道的每一道光
都在流转。

惟独众光之父，
在他并没有转动的影儿。

今晨在你手中的每一件美物——
日用的饼、呼吸的气息、身旁的朋友——
都降自那双
永不改变心意的手。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 如果今天这幅《没有转动的影儿》（雅各书 1:16–17）就挂在你清晨出门的门旁，它最后那句——“今晨在你手中的每一件美物——日用的饼、呼吸的气息、身旁的朋友——都降自那双永不改变心意的手”——会如何塑造你今天的选择？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “各样美善的恩赐和各样全备的赏赐都是从上头来的，从众光之父那里降下来的”

paintings.title: the mirror
paintings.epigraph: “he is like a man looking at his natural face in a mirror”
paintings.poem:
you glance in the bronze mirror,
see the smudge on your cheek,
and walk out the door
without wiping it.

that is hearing
without doing.

the word is not a mirror
to admire.
it is a basin of water
set beside it.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Every stop on the Pilgrim Walk shows how God meets us in ordinary places (James 1:22–25)—where in your own home or work today does “it is a basin of water set beside it” ring true?
paintings.zh_poem:
你朝铜镜里瞥了一眼，
看见脸颊上的污痕，
却没有擦拭，
便径直走出门去。

这就是单单听道
而不行道。

神的道不是一面
供人顾影自怜的镜子；
它是摆在镜旁的一盆清水。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 天路同行的每一站都向我们显明，神如何在平凡之处与我们相遇（雅各书 1:22–25）——今天在你的家中或工作里，哪一处让你深感“它是摆在镜旁的一盆清水”的真实？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “就像人对着镜子看自己本来的面目”

paintings.title: a knock on the door
paintings.epigraph: “to visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction”
paintings.poem:
he boils religion down
to a knock on a door.

the widow no one visits.
the child no one claims.

bring bread.
sit a while.
come back next week.

and keep your own hands clean
on the way there.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Take a slow breath and read the final line again: “and keep your own hands clean on the way there.” How would you walk through the next hour differently if you carried that truth with you?
paintings.zh_poem:
他把虔诚浓缩成
门前的一声轻叩。

那个无人探望的寡妇。
那个无人认领的孤儿。

带点饼去。
坐上一会儿。
下周再来。

并且在前往的路上，
保守自己的双手洁净，不沾世俗。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 深吸一口气，再读一遍最后那行诗：“并且在前往的路上，保守自己的双手洁净，不沾世俗。”如果你带着这份真理走入接下来的一个小时，你的脚步会有何不同？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “在神我们的父面前，那清洁没有玷污的虔诚，就是看顾在患难中的孤儿寡妇”

paintings.title: the good seat
paintings.epigraph: “Sit here in a good place”
paintings.poem:
a gold ring walks in,
and someone jumps up:
here, sit here.

a man in dirty clothes walks in:
you can stand.
or the floor is fine.

we do it without thinking.
James says:
think.

the King you worship
was laid in a feeding trough
and never once
asked for the good seat.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Think of a season when you knew the feeling of “a gold ring walks in, and someone jumps up: here, sit here.” Looking through the lens of James 2:1–4, what does it mean to discover that “the King you worship was laid in a feeding trough and never once asked for the good seat”?
paintings.zh_poem:
一个戴金戒指的人走进来，
立刻有人起身招呼：
请，请坐在这好位上。

一个穿脏衣服的穷人走进来：
你站在那里吧，
或者坐在我脚凳下也行。

我们往往不假思索地这样做。
雅各说：
想一想吧。

你所敬拜的那位君王，
降生时卧在喂牲口的槽里，
一生中从不曾
索要过一次好位子。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 回想一段你曾体会过“一个戴金戒指的人走进来，立刻有人起身招呼：请，请坐在这好位上”的时光。透过雅各书 2:1–4 的眼光，发现“你所敬拜的那位君王，降生时卧在喂牲口的槽里，一生中从不曾索要过一次好位子”对你意味着什么？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “请坐在这好位上”

paintings.title: rich
paintings.epigraph: “Didn’t God choose those who are poor in this world to be rich in faith”
paintings.poem:
look again at the poor man
you asked to stand.

God may have chosen him
first.

heir to a kingdom.
rich
in the only coin
that spends in heaven.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Look closely at the quiet centerpiece of “rich” in this painting (James 2:5)—if you could leave one anxious weight beside it today, what would you set down?
paintings.zh_poem:
再看一眼那个被你叫去站着的
贫穷人吧。

神或许最先拣选的，
正是他。

他是天国的后嗣，
拥有天上唯一通用的货币——
在信上无比富足。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 细看这幅画中《在信上富足》那安静的画面中心（雅各书 2:5）——如果今天你可以把一件焦虑的重担放在它旁边，你会放下什么？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “神岂不是拣选了世上的贫穷人，叫他们在信上富足”

paintings.title: mercy wins
paintings.epigraph: “Mercy triumphs over judgment.”
paintings.poem:
you will be judged
by the same measure
you used on others,

so use a generous one.

in the courtroom of God,
mercy has the last word.
it always
wins the case.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Let your eyes rest on the brushwork and light around the quiet centerpiece of “mercy wins”: what quiet prayer rises in you when you read, “you will be judged by the same measure you used on others, so use a generous one. it always wins the case”?
paintings.zh_poem:
你用怎样的量器
去量别人，
自己也必受怎样的审判，

所以，当用宽宏的量器。

在神的法庭上，
怜悯拥有最终的定音。
它总是
赢得胜诉。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 让目光停留在画中《怜悯向审判夸胜》那安静的画面中心：当你读到“你用怎样的量器去量别人，自己也必受怎样的审判，所以，当用宽宏的量器……它总是赢得胜诉”时，你心中升起怎样安静的祷告？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “怜悯原是向审判夸胜。”

paintings.title: be warmed and filled
paintings.epigraph: “Go in peace. Be warmed and filled”
paintings.poem:
go in peace, we say.
stay warm.
eat well.

and close the door.

a blessing with no bread in it
is just weather.

faith that feeds no one
is a body
with no breath.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Linger with the movement in “be warmed and filled” (James 2:14–17) from “go in peace, we say” to “faith that feeds no one is a body with no breath”—where do you find yourself along that arc today?
paintings.zh_poem:
我们嘴上说：平平安安地去吧，
愿你穿得暖，
吃得饱——

随后便关上了门。

一句没有饼的祝福，
不过是一阵耳旁风。

不给饥饿者喂饱的信心，
就像没有气息的身体。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在《得暖吃饱》（雅各书 2:14–17）中细细品味那份转折——从“我们嘴上说：平平安安地去吧”到“不给饥饿者喂饱的信心，就像没有气息的身体”——今天你发现自己处在这段弧线的哪个位置？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “平平安安地去吧！愿你们穿得暖，吃得饱”

paintings.title: they shudder
paintings.epigraph: “The demons also believe, and shudder.”
paintings.poem:
you believe God is one?
good.

so do the demons,
and they shudder.

believing the right facts
is where faith starts,
not where it lives.

faith lives
in what you do
on an ordinary Tuesday.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Notice how “they shudder” (James 2:18–20) arrives at: “faith lives in what you do on an ordinary Tuesday.” Who in your life is walking a hard stretch of road today and needs you to share this grace with them?
paintings.zh_poem:
你信神只有一位？
你信的不错。

鬼魔也信，
却是战惊。

承认正确的道理，
只是信心的起点，
而不是信心栖居的地方。

信心活在
你在每一个平凡日子里
亲手所行的事中。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 留意《鬼魔也信，却是战惊》（雅各书 2:18–20）如何落脚于：“信心活在你在每一个平凡日子里亲手所行的事中。”今天在你的生命中，有谁正走在一程艰难的路上，需要你与他们分享这份恩典？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “鬼魔也信，却是战惊。”

paintings.title: friend of God
paintings.epigraph: “he was called the friend of God”
paintings.poem:
Abraham believed God,
and it was counted to him
as righteousness.

then he got up
and walked it out—
tent to tent,
year after year,
all the way to the mountain.

that is why they called him
not the believer,
not the scholar,
but the friend of God.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: What if the most important thing you remember before tonight is the quiet lesson of James 2:21–23: “that is why they called him not the believer, not the scholar, but the friend of God”?
paintings.zh_poem:
亚伯拉罕信神，
这就算为他的义。

随后他起身，
一步一步将这信心走了出来——
从一座帐棚到另一座帐棚，
年复一年，
一直走到摩利亚山上。

正因如此，人称他
不只是信徒，
也不只是学者，
而是神的朋友。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 如果在今晚入睡前，你最需要记住的是雅各书 2:21–23 那安静的启示：“正因如此，人称他不只是信徒，也不只是学者，而是神的朋友”——这会带给你怎样的看见？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “他又得称为神的朋友。”

paintings.title: we all stumble
paintings.epigraph: “For we all stumble in many things.”
paintings.poem:
we all stumble,
says the teacher,
putting himself in the we.

that's the first lesson
before you teach:

you are not above the path.
you are on it,
with a scraped knee
like everyone else.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Imagine standing inside this frame beside the quiet centerpiece of “we all stumble”: what hurry or noise in your week begins to fade when you hear, “you are on it, with a scraped knee like everyone else”?
paintings.zh_title: 原来我们在许多事上都有过失
paintings.zh_poem:
作师傅的雅各说：
原来我们在许多事上都有过失——
他把自己也放进了“我们”之中。

这就是教导别人之前的
第一课：

你并不是高高凌驾于道路之上；
你也走在路上，
和众人一样，
膝盖上也带着跌倒的擦伤。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 想象自己站在这幅画框里、守在《原来我们在许多事上都有过失》那安静的画面中心：当你听见“你也走在路上，和众人一样，膝盖上也带着跌倒的擦伤”时，你这一周里的哪些匆忙与喧嚣开始渐渐消退？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “原来我们在许多事上都有过失。”

paintings.title: small things steer
paintings.epigraph: “guided by a very small rudder, wherever the pilot desires”
paintings.poem:
a bit of iron
turns a horse.
a slab of wood
turns a ship in the wind.

small things steer.

and the smallest steering thing you own
is behind your teeth.

where is it
taking you?
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Read the closing words aloud in the stillness: “small things steer. where is it taking you?.” What part of your heart feels most searched or comforted by James 3:3–4 right now?
paintings.zh_poem:
一小块嚼环
能调动骏马。
一块小小的木舵
能在狂风中调转大船。

微小的器物掌管方向。

而你身上最小的舵，
就藏在你的齿唇之间。

此刻，它正把你
带往何方？
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在静默中轻声读出结尾的诗句：“微小的器物掌管方向……此刻，它正把你带往何方？”此刻，雅各书 3:3–4 最触动或最安慰你内心的是哪一部分？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “只用小小的舵，就随着掌舵的意思转动。”

paintings.title: one spark
paintings.epigraph: “See how a small fire can spread to a large forest!”
paintings.poem:
one spark in dry brush.
by evening,
the whole hillside.

one sentence
said in a hot moment,
and a friendship,
a family,
a church,
is smoke.

words are small.
so is an ember.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: In James 3:5–6, grace meets us right beside the quiet centerpiece of “one spark”: how does the closing thought—“words are small. so is an ember”—steady your footing for the road ahead?
paintings.zh_poem:
干柴里的一点火星，
到了傍晚，
便烧遍整座山坡。

气头上脱口而出的
一句话，
便叫一段情谊、
一个家庭、
一间教会，
化作焦烟。

言语虽小，
炭火也是如此。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在雅各书 3:5–6 中，恩典就在《一点星火》那安静的画面中心与我们相遇：结尾的深思——“言语虽小，炭火也是如此”——如何为你前面的道路稳住脚步？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “看哪，最小的火能点着最大的树林！”

paintings.title: no one can tame it
paintings.epigraph: “Out of the same mouth comes blessing and cursing.”
paintings.poem:
we have tamed
beasts and birds,
creatures of the sea.

but no one
has tamed the tongue.

one morning it sings to God.
by afternoon it cuts down
someone made
in his image.

these things,
my brothers,
ought not to be so.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: If today’s painting of “no one can tame it” (James 3:7–10) hung beside the door you walk out of this morning, how would its final line—“these things, my brothers, ought not to be so”—shape your choices?
paintings.zh_poem:
我们已经制伏了
走兽与飞禽，
以及海里的水族。

惟独舌头，
没有人能制伏。

清晨它向神歌颂，
到了午后，它却砍伤那个
照着神形像所造的人。

我的弟兄们，
这是不应当的。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 如果今天这幅《没有人能制伏》（雅各书 3:7–10）就挂在你清晨出门的门旁，它最后那句——“我的弟兄们，这是不应当的”——会如何塑造你今天的选择？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “颂赞和咒诅从一个口里出来！”

paintings.title: the spring
paintings.epigraph: “Does a spring send out from the same opening fresh and bitter water?”
paintings.poem:
a spring gives one kind of water.
a fig tree gives figs.
a vine doesn't wake up
and try olives.

what comes out of you
tells what is in you.

so don't just watch your words.
ask God
to change the water
at the source.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Every stop on the Pilgrim Walk shows how God meets us in ordinary places (James 3:11–12)—where in your own home or work today does “ask God to change the water at the source” ring true?
paintings.zh_poem:
一口泉眼只涌出一种水。
无花果树只结无花果。
葡萄树绝不会一觉醒来
试着结出橄榄。

从你口中流露出来的，
显明你里面装的是什么。

所以，不要只盯着自己的言辞；
求神从源头处
更换那口泉水吧。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 天路同行的每一站都向我们显明，神如何在平凡之处与我们相遇（雅各书 3:11–12）——今天在你的家中或工作里，哪一处让你深感“求神从源头处更换那口泉水吧”的真实？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “泉源从一个眼里能发出甜苦两样水吗？”

paintings.title: sown in peace
paintings.epigraph: “the fruit of righteousness is sown in peace by those who make peace.”
paintings.poem:
there is a kind of smart
that climbs over people.

and there is wisdom from above:
peaceable. gentle.
willing to listen.
full of mercy.
without a mask.

it doesn't win arguments.
it plants.
and what it plants in peace
comes up
as righteousness.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Take a slow breath and read the final line again: “and what it plants in peace comes up as righteousness.” How would you walk through the next hour differently if you carried that truth with you?
paintings.zh_poem:
有一种聪明，
总想踩在别人头上。

但那从上头来的智慧：
先是清洁，后是和平，
温良柔顺，乐意倾听，
满有怜悯，
没有假冒的面具。

它不靠争辩取胜，
它只管栽种；
凡它用和平所栽种的，
长出来便是公义的果子。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 深吸一口气，再读一遍最后那行诗：“凡它用和平所栽种的，长出来便是公义的果子。”如果你带着这份真理走入接下来的一个小时，你的脚步会有何不同？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “并且使人和平的，是用和平所栽种的义果。”

paintings.title: open hands
paintings.epigraph: “Y ou don’t have, because you don’t ask.”
paintings.poem:
where do the fights come from?
from wanting,
and wanting,
and not having.

we grab.
we scheme.
we elbow.

and never once
simply ask.

and when we do,
it's for more
to spend on ourselves.

open hands, James says.
open to him first.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Think of a season when you knew the feeling of “where do the fights come from?.” Looking through the lens of James 4:1–3, what does it mean to discover that “open hands, James says. open to him first”?
paintings.zh_poem:
争战斗殴是从哪里来的呢？
是从贪恋、
切慕、
却得不着来的。

我们抓取，
我们算计，
我们推搡。

却从来不曾
单纯地向神求。

即便求了，
也只是为了浪费在自己的宴乐上。

雅各说：摊开双手吧，
先向着他敞开。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 回想一段你曾体会过“争战斗殴是从哪里来的呢”那种焦躁争夺的时光。透过雅各书 4:1–3 的眼光，发现“雅各说：摊开双手吧，先向着他敞开”对你意味着什么？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “你们得不着，是因为你们不求。”

paintings.title: more grace
paintings.epigraph: “But he gives more grace.”
paintings.poem:
he gives more grace.

three words
for every time
you thought you'd used it up.

and it runs the way water does—
downhill,
to the lowest place.

God resists the proud.
the humble
get flooded.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Look closely at the quiet centerpiece of “more grace” in this painting (James 4:6)—if you could leave one anxious weight beside it today, what would you set down?
paintings.zh_poem:
他赐更多的恩典——

短短一句话，
回应你每一次以为
恩典已经用尽的时刻。

这恩典如同流水——
总是顺着山坡往下流，
流向最低微的地方。

神阻挡骄傲的人，
谦卑的人
却被恩典漫溢。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 细看这幅画中《更多的恩典》那安静的画面中心（雅各书 4:6）——如果今天你可以把一件焦虑的重担放在它旁边，你会放下什么？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “但他赐更多的恩典。”

paintings.title: come close
paintings.epigraph: “Cleanse your hands, you sinners.”
paintings.poem:
come close to God,
and he comes close to you.

it's not a long road.
it's a turn of the body,
a step,
a basin of water,
washed hands,
a heart made single again.

he was always
nearer
than your running.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Let your eyes rest on the brushwork and light around your own two hands: what quiet prayer rises in you when you read, “he was always nearer than your running”?
paintings.zh_poem:
你们亲近神，
神就必亲近你们。

这不是一条漫长的路。
只是一个转身，
迈出一步，
一盆清水，
洗净双手，
让心再次归于专一。

他一直
比你奔逃的脚步
离你更近。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 让目光停留在画中围绕着双手的笔触与光线：当你读到“他一直比你奔逃的脚步离你更近”时，你心中升起怎样安静的祷告？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “有罪的人哪，要洁净你们的手！”

paintings.title: the chair
paintings.epigraph: “But who are you to judge another?”
paintings.poem:
when you speak against your brother,
you climb into a chair
that isn't yours.

there is one lawgiver.
one judge.
one who can save.

get down from the chair.
sit next to your brother
on the floor.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Linger with the movement in “the chair” (James 4:11–12) from “when you speak against your brother, you climb into a chair that isn't yours” to “sit next to your brother on the floor”—where do you find yourself along that arc today?
paintings.zh_poem:
当你批评弟兄的时候，
你便爬上了那把
不属于你的座椅。

设立律法的只有一位，
判断人的只有一位，
能救人能灭人的也只有一位。

从那把椅子上下来吧，
坐在你弟兄身旁的
地板上。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在《审判的座位》（雅各书 4:11–12）中细细品味那份转折——从“当你批评弟兄的时候，你便爬上了那把不属于你的座椅”到“从那把椅子上下来吧，坐在你弟兄身旁的地板上”——今天你发现自己处在这段弧线的哪个位置？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “你是谁，竟敢论断别人呢？”

paintings.title: mist
paintings.epigraph: “For you are a vapor that appears for a little time, and then vanishes away.”
paintings.poem:
tomorrow we'll go to the city,
spend a year,
make a profit—

and the morning mist
lifts off the valley
while we're still talking.

you are mist.
beautiful, brief,
already rising.

so say it the humble way:
if the Lord wills,
we will live,
and do this or that.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Notice how “mist” (James 4:13–15) arrives at: “so say it the humble way: if the Lord wills, we will live, and do this or that.” Who in your life is walking a hard stretch of road today and needs you to share this grace with them?
paintings.zh_poem:
明天我们要往某城去，
在那里住一年，
做买卖得利——

我们话音未落，
山谷里的晨雾
已悄然散去。

你原来是一片云雾：
美丽，短暂，
转瞬消散。

所以当存谦卑的心这样说：
主若愿意，
我们就可以活着，
也可以做这事，或做那事。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 留意《一片云雾》（雅各书 4:13–15）如何落脚于：“所以当存谦卑的心这样说：主若愿意，我们就可以活着，也可以做这事，或做那事。”今天在你的生命中，有谁正走在一程艰难的路上，需要你与他们分享这份恩典？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “你们原来是一片云雾，出现少时就不见了。”

paintings.title: the good you know
paintings.epigraph: “To him therefore who knows to do good, and doesn’t do it, to him it is sin.”
paintings.poem:
not the wrong you did.
the good you knew
and walked past.

the visit you didn't make.
the gate you didn't mend.
the name you didn't pray.

James counts those too.

and grace
counts them first,
then hands you the hammer.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: What if the most important thing you remember before tonight is the quiet lesson of James 4:17: “and grace counts them first, then hands you the hammer”?
paintings.zh_poem:
不只是你做错的事，
还有你明明知道该行的善，
却擦肩走过。

那次没有去的探望，
那扇没有修补的篱门，
那个没有在祷告中提起的名字。

雅各把这些也算在账上。

而恩典
先替你承担了这笔账，
再把修门的锤子递回你手中。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 如果在今晚入睡前，你最需要记住的是雅各书 4:17 那安静的启示：“而恩典先替你承担了这笔账，再把修门的锤子递回你手中”——这会给你带来怎样的激励？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “人若知道行善，却不去行，这就是他的罪了。”

paintings.title: moth-eaten
paintings.epigraph: “your garments are moth-eaten”
paintings.poem:
the fine robe folded in the chest
for a day that never came.
the moths found it first.

and in the field
the reapers you never paid
are crying out—

and heaven, James says,
has ears.

what you hoard
rots.
what you withhold
testifies.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Imagine standing inside this frame beside the quiet centerpiece of “moth-eaten”: what hurry or noise in your week begins to fade when you hear, “what you withhold testifies”?
paintings.zh_poem:
那件叠在箱子里、
留待某个从未到来之日的华美外袍，
已被虫子抢先咬破。

而在田野里，
那些替你收割、却被你亏欠工钱的人
正在喊冤——

雅各说：
天上的主已经听见了。

凡你囤积的，
终必朽坏；
凡你扣留的，
都要作见证告你。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 想象自己站在这幅画框里、守在《虫子咬了》那安静的画面中心：当你听见“凡你囤积的，终必朽坏；凡你扣留的，都要作见证告你”时，你这一周里的哪些匆忙与喧嚣开始渐渐消退？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “你们的衣服被虫子咬了。”

paintings.title: the farmer
paintings.epigraph: “Establish your hearts, for the coming of the Lord is at hand.”
paintings.poem:
the farmer can't hurry the barley.
he plants,
and then he waits
for the autumn rain,
and waits
for the spring rain.

he doesn't dig up the seed
to check on it.

be like that.
steady your heart.
what God has planted
is coming up
on God's time.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Read the closing words aloud in the stillness: “what God has planted is coming up on God's time.” What part of your heart feels most searched or comforted by James 5:7–8 right now?
paintings.zh_poem:
农夫催不快地里的大麦。
他播下种子，
随后耐心等候
秋雨降下，
又耐心等候
春雨临到。

他不会把种子刨出来
看它长了没有。

你也要像他那样：
坚固你的心。
神所栽种的，
必按神的时候
破土而出。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在静默中轻声读出结尾的诗句：“神所栽种的，必按神的时候破土而出。”此刻，雅各书 5:7–8 最触动或最安慰你内心的是哪一部分？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “你们也当忍耐，坚固你们的心，因为主来的日子近了。”

paintings.title: the end of the story
paintings.epigraph: “the Lord is full of compassion and mercy.”
paintings.poem:
you've heard of Job:
the ashes, the losses,
the long argument with heaven.

and you've seen the end of the story,
what the Lord did at the last.

endurance is not
pretending it doesn't hurt.
it is still being there
at the end,
where he is full
of compassion
and mercy.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: In James 5:10–11, grace meets us right beside the quiet centerpiece of “the end of the story”: how does the closing thought—“it is still being there at the end, where he is full of compassion and mercy”—steady your footing for the road ahead?
paintings.zh_poem:
你们听见过约伯的忍耐：
炉灰、丧失，
以及与上天漫长的诉说。

你们也看见了故事的结局，
看见主至终怎样待他。

忍耐并不是
假装一点也不痛；
而是熬到结局来临时
依然还在那里——
在那里，主满心怜悯，
大有慈悲。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在雅各书 5:10–11 中，恩典就在《给他的结局》那安静的画面中心与我们相遇：结尾的深思——“而是熬到结局来临时依然还在那里——在那里，主满心怜悯，大有慈悲”——如何为你前面的道路稳住脚步？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “并且知道主是满心怜悯，大有慈悲。”

paintings.title: pray, sing
paintings.epigraph: “Is any among you suffering? Let him pray. Is any cheerful? Let him sing praises.”
paintings.poem:
is anyone hurting? pray.
is anyone happy? sing.
is anyone sick?
call the elders.
bring the oil.

confess to each other.
pray for each other.

this is how
the first churches
carried each other:
honesty,
oil,
and one another.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: If today’s painting of “pray, sing” (James 5:13–16) hung beside the door you walk out of this morning, how would its final line—“this is how the first churches carried each other: honesty, oil, and one another”—shape your choices?
paintings.zh_poem:
有人受苦吗？他就该祷告。
有人喜乐吗？他就该歌颂。
有人病了吗？
他就该请教会的长老来，
奉主的名用油抹他。

要彼此认罪，
互相代求。

初代的教会
正是这样彼此扶持的：
诚实、
膏油、
以及彼此相顾。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 如果今天这幅《该祷告、该歌颂》（雅各书 5:13–16）就挂在你清晨出门的门旁，它最后那句——“初代的教会正是这样彼此扶持的：诚实、膏油、以及彼此相顾”——会如何塑造你今天的选择？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “你们中间有受苦的呢，他就该祷告；有喜乐的呢，他就该歌颂。”

paintings.title: like us
paintings.epigraph: “Elijah was a man with a nature like ours”
paintings.poem:
Elijah was just like us,
James says—
same fears,
same moods,
same kind of knees.

and he prayed,
and the sky shut.
and he prayed again,
and the rain came,
and the ground turned green.

don't wait to become a giant
before you pray.
the giants
were ordinary people
who asked.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Every stop on the Pilgrim Walk shows how God meets us in ordinary places (James 5:17–18)—where in your own home or work today does “the giants were ordinary people who asked” ring true?
paintings.zh_title: 与我们是一样性情的人
paintings.zh_poem:
雅各说：
以利亚与我们是一样性情的人——
有同样的惧怕，
同样的起伏，
同样会发酸的双膝。

但他恳切祷告，
天就闭塞不下雨；
他又祷告，
天就降下雨来，
地也生出土产。

不要等到自己成了伟人
才去祷告。
那些信心的伟人，
不过是开口祈求的
平凡人。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 天路同行的每一站都向我们显明，神如何在平凡之处与我们相遇（雅各书 5:17–18）——今天在你的家中或工作里，哪一处让你深感“那些信心的伟人，不过是开口祈求的平凡人”的真实？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “以利亚与我们是一样性情的人”

paintings.title: bring them home
paintings.epigraph: “he who turns a sinner from the error of his way will save a soul from death”
paintings.poem:
and the letter ends
not with a blessing
but with a search party.

if someone wanders,
go after them.

bring them home,
and love
covers a multitude of sins
the way a coat covers
a cold child
on the long walk back.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Take a slow breath and read the final line again: “bring them home, and love covers a multitude of sins the way a coat covers a cold child on the long walk back.” How would you walk through the next hour differently if you carried that truth with you?
paintings.zh_poem:
全信的结尾，
不是一句礼仪性的祝祷，
而是一支外出寻人的队伍。

若有人失迷真道，
去把他找回来吧。

领他回家，
而爱能遮掩许多的罪，
就像在漫长的归途上，
用一件外衣
裹住受冻的孩子。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 深吸一口气，再读一遍最后那行诗：“领他回家，而爱能遮掩许多的罪，就像在漫长的归途上，用一件外衣裹住受冻的孩子。”如果你带着这份真理走入接下来的一个小时，你的脚步会有何不同？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “这人该知道：叫一个罪人从迷路上转回，便是救一个灵魂不死”

zh_beforeYouBegin:
雅各书是一封充满质朴智慧的短简：谈及百般的试炼与忍耐、富足的与卑微的、有行为的信心、能点着树林的舌头，以及耐心等候秋雨春雨的农夫。

本书以三十首短诗走过这五章经文。每首诗旁配有一幅画，上方引有一句经文；你可以在一个夜晚一口气读完，也可以每个清晨慢读一页。

这些诗并非圣经本身，只是一个读经的人对经文的回应。请翻开雅各书与本书一同阅读，让神真实的话语作最终的定音。
